sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Basis**: EIA is mandated under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, specifically through the **EIA Notification 2006** (superseding 1994).
• **Core Objective**: To integrate environmental concerns into the developmental planning process at the **pre-investment stage**.
• **Key Stages**: Screening, Scoping, Public Consultation, and Appraisal.
• **Key Metric**: The **Environmental Clearance (EC)** is the final legal instrument granted by the MoEFCC or SEIAA, without which a project cannot commence.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Large-scale, high-impact projects (e.g., Nuclear, Ports, Highways > 100km).
Appraised at the Central level by the Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC).
Prelims: Focus on the 'Central' authority vs 'State' authority.
Appraised at the State level by the State Level Environment Appraisal Committee (SEAC).

items.definition: A mandatory process where the project proponent must disclose the EIA report to the public and hold a hearing. It is a critical check against 'top-down' development.
A body of experts constituted by the MoEFCC to evaluate Category A projects and provide recommendations for granting or rejecting EC.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **PARIVESH Portal**: Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub for automated EC tracking.
• **Post-Clearance Monitoring**: Ensuring compliance with the conditions stipulated in the EC through the Regional Offices of MoEFCC.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Poor quality of EIA reports (outsourced to consultants), lack of public participation transparency, and 'Post-facto' clearance issues.
• **Solutions**: Strengthening the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), mandatory independent audits, and digitizing the baseline data collection.

items.title: Mnemonic for EIA Stages
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'SS-PA' (Super Star, Public Appeal).
• **Decoded Meaning**: S-Screening, S-Scoping, P-Public Consultation, A-Appraisal.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'EIA Notification 2006' as a law passed by Parliament. It is a 'Subordinate Legislation' (Delegated Legislation) under the EPA 1986.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Procedural Democracy' when discussing the importance of Public Consultation in EIA.

keyTakeaways: EIA is not a law itself but a notification issued under the EPA, 1986.
Public Consultation is mandatory for most projects but can be exempted for strategic/defense projects.
The 'Precautionary Principle' is the legal bedrock of the EIA process.
